arguments.mode: Library mode or CLI --mode: web (default), macos, windows, inspect. Select only the prerequisites you need.

doctor.result: JSON status=ready or failed, ready boolean, selected mode, individual checks with paths/versions and actionable errors, limitations and model_calls=0. CLI exits 1 if any required check fails.
doctor.failures: Missing or unrunnable ffmpeg/ffprobe, missing libx264 for recording, missing Chromium or selected native companion, or unsupported native platform. Fix the reported dependency and rerun doctor. No request_id is needed. Installing Showrun or running prepare-runtime does not install FFmpeg. macOS/Homebrew: brew install ffmpeg. Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install ffmpeg. Windows/winget: winget install --id Gyan.FFmpeg --exact. Otherwise obtain a build from https://ffmpeg.org/download.html. Put both executables on the calling process PATH, restart its terminal/agent/service, and verify ffmpeg -version and ffprobe -version.
doctor.guidance: Read-only, provider-free probes: FFmpeg and ffprobe paths and runnable versions; recording modes also require libx264. Web checks the Playwright driver and Chromium file without launching a browser. Native modes check only the selected platform and companion file; use desktop-status separately for permissions/session access (it launches the companion). Inspect checks only media tools, not libx264 or capture backends. Does not install anything, reserve a take, launch a target/companion, access media or initialize an Agent. Runtime preparation, credentials, browser OS libraries, native permissions/session and actual capture remain unchecked; ready refers only to listed checks. Library: Showrun.doctor(mode='web').

manifest.result: Canonical frontmatter, body and capabilities as JSON.
manifest.failures: Broken installation: reinstall. No provider needed.
manifest.guidance: Reads packaged metadata only; no credentials, target, browser or FFmpeg required. Library: Showrun.manifest().

arguments.request: Library dict; CLI JSON filename. Required identity, target, starting_state, ordered steps, authority; optional context and capture.

validate.result: status=valid and effective public request, or invalid_request error.
validate.failures: Unknown fields, unsupported target/action authority, invalid geometry or limits. Correct input. No provider needed.
validate.guidance: Checks structure only; it does not check target readiness or execute UI actions. No credentials, browser or FFmpeg required. Library: Showrun().validate(request). Before recording, prepare the starting state and inspect the effective request.

arguments.request: Same dict/file as validate. For generic URL targets, navigation_only=false and authority.ui={actions:[click,fill,select,check,scroll,key],allowed_values:[...],target_effects:all_in_session} explicitly authorize target-session effects. Narrower backend limits must be enforced by the target. Generic field assertions check label plus value or checked state. Without ui, legacy navigation-only remains the default. Optional authority.stories_comment={story_id,revision_id,text} with navigation_only=false enables one exact UI comment on a fresh prepared managed fixture. Steps accept visible_text and/or assertions (control visibility, managed review_panel visibility, retained_comment). Comment grants require retained_comment evidence. Optional capture.audio={output: application|system, include_bundle_ids?, microphone?, microphone_device?, require_signal?=true} records sound for macos targets only; absent means silent footage and an unchanged request fingerprint.
arguments.storage: Library constructor or CLI --storage: retained operation and artifact root.
arguments.model: Constructor dict {provider, model, credential_env?, response_tokens?, reasoning_effort?}. response_tokens: integer 512–4096, default 2048 per call. OpenAI reasoning_effort: low (default for reasoning models), medium or high; unsupported model parameters fail. CLI --provider, --model, --credential-env uses default inference controls. Explicit provider/model required. Direct provider.complete inside a restricted Agent session; no stock session.execute loop.

record.result: Retained receipt with status, per-step outcomes, usage, resources, cleanup, partial flag and optional verified media. A completed step with no UI interaction has outcome=satisfied_without_action and warning code=step_satisfied_without_action, also listed in receipt.warnings. initial_result_satisfied distinguishes an initially true check from later observation-only completion. Success remains valid for observation-only steps; visible text does not prove fresh execution.
record.failures: Missing credentials/runtime/capture dependencies; target not ready; refused actions; limits; missing destination; failed hold/capture/cleanup. Run the doctor capability with --mode web (or macos/windows for native), and follow each dependency's installation/PATH remedy; showrun doctor --help includes platform installation commands. Installing Showrun and prepare-runtime do not install FFmpeg. Exact retry never executes again. Inspect the retained failed take, correct prerequisites and starting state, and deliberately use a new request_id for another recording. Audio: audio_unsupported, audio_unavailable, audio_permission_missing, audio_device_not_found, audio_start_failed, audio_interrupted, audio_no_signal, audio_failed; footage stays retained and labeled.
record.guidance: Library: Showrun(storage, model).record(request). Run doctor for capture prerequisites, and prepare-runtime in this installation. Supply a concrete provider/model with credentials in the process environment, a prepared target and starting_state, ordered steps and bounded authority. URL targets stay caller-owned; managed Stories fixtures come from prepare-fixture. UI actions/disclosure and target spending require separate grants. Assertions already true can satisfy steps without actions: read the outcome/warnings, check changed state and inspect decoded footage. wait_for_result=true observes without further input or model calls. Exact retries return retained outcomes; retakes require new IDs. Web needs Chromium and FFmpeg/ffprobe; native capture needs FFmpeg/ffprobe and a prepared companion/window. macOS 14+ uses the pinned desktop-v0.6.0 companion, including explicit terminal type/key grants; type appends and Enter is separate. The documented Terminal.app trial is not universal terminal compatibility. Windows desktop-v0.2.0 supports experimental click/fill, not terminal mode. Pause user input during native takes; sampled footage has no cursor and is not desktop isolation. Audio is opt-in via capture.audio on macOS targets (ScreenCaptureKit; web/Windows fail with audio_unsupported): read receipt.audio for sources, sample rate/channels, per-source and final-track signal (present/silent/none_received), sync and permission gaps. Missing companion capability or permission fails before input; no signal fails the take unless require_signal=false. Run desktop-status for permissions and reported companion metadata; older binaries report metadata as unknown. See the full guide's native, terminal, text-entry and timing sections for request shapes, resize_to_capture and platform limits.

status.result: Retained receipt plus cancellation acknowledgment; crashed owner may be uncertain.
status.failures: not_found: correct store and identity. No model, target or browser calls.
status.guidance: Reads the selected store without contacting the target, model or browser. Library: Showrun(storage).status(request_id). Use the same storage as record. Poll until terminal after cancellation; uncertain owner state needs inspection, not automatic replay.

inspect.result: Receipt with newly inspected hash and decoded media metadata, or restricted notice.
inspect.failures: Missing/changed/invalid artifact or missing/unusable FFmpeg/ffprobe. Run showrun doctor --mode inspect and follow its installation/PATH remedies; showrun doctor --help includes platform installation commands. Inspection does not need libx264. After dependency repair, retry inspect with the same take/request_id; no new recording is needed. Preserve earlier receipts; do not replay. No model calls.
inspect.guidance: Requires FFmpeg/ffprobe to decode retained media; no model, target or browser needed. Library: Showrun(storage).inspect(request_id). Use the recording store. Integrity checks do not establish that the demo is readable or semantically correct; review the actual footage.

cancel.result: cancellation_requested; not cleanup proof and not rollback.
cancel.failures: not_found: correct store and identity. For crashed owner, inspect resources manually. No model calls.
cancel.guidance: Requests cancellation of a running record in the same store. Library: Showrun(storage).cancel(request_id). It does not undo target effects or spending. Read status until terminal and check cleanup; never infer that acknowledgment means processes have exited.

arguments.presentation: Library dict or CLI JSON file: title, html, sources?, purpose?, audience?. Retained source fields are filtered to Stories' public import shape.
arguments.destination: Absolute fresh empty caller-owned directory; never an existing store or symlink.

prepare-fixture.result: status=prepared, supplied_sha256 and exact target including story_id, revision_id and fixture_sha256. Use this target unchanged for managed recording.
prepare-fixture.failures: fixture_invalid or stories_missing: preserve any partial import, select a new empty destination after correcting the supplied content or installation. No model, dashboard or live-store reads.
prepare-fixture.guidance: Requires an installed Stories 0.1.0 Python interpreter and an absent or empty destination with an existing parent. Library: Showrun.prepare_fixture(presentation, destination, python). Imports supplied title/HTML and supported source metadata through public Stories APIs, without launching a dashboard or model. Media and structured documents are outside this fixture path. Use the returned target unchanged; record later starts and stops its isolated dashboard. Existing stores and symlinks are refused.

prepare-runtime.result: Prepared local Agent snapshot keyed by interpreter, prefix, Python/Agent version and bundle identity; model_calls=0. Other installations do not replace this snapshot.
prepare-runtime.failures: Setup requires network/dependency access. Explicitly rerun setup after correcting it. No inference or target launch.
prepare-runtime.guidance: Explicit setup may fetch Agent modules and write a local runtime snapshot. It does not call a model, install FFmpeg/ffprobe or Chromium, or start a target. Run showrun doctor for capture dependency guidance. Library: Showrun.prepare_runtime(). Run in the same installed interpreter that will record; another environment’s preparation does not transfer.

arguments.storage: Library constructor or CLI --storage: one configured retained take root. Review metadata is stored separately under .showrun-review.
arguments.workspace: Explicit versioned review workspace ID; the default is default. Remote-facing service/CLI/MCP calls may also provide explicit --demo scope.
arguments.operations: state, list, demo, take, clip, select, rename, prepare-delete, delete, draft, note, notes, playback, appearance, begin-intent, ack-intent, reject-intent, mp4, zip or serve. Intent admission accepts --kind and --payload JSON; acknowledgment and rejection target an exact intent ID. Exports refuse to overwrite an existing destination.

review.result: Provider-free retained demos/takes/clips, exact selection state, receipt outcomes, notes, durable request/CAS mutation receipts or original-byte downloads.
review.failures: Missing or changed receipts/media, restricted/unfinalized clips, stale versions, active-work deletion, out-of-scope IDs, missing exact confirmation, incomplete/uncertain cleanup, revoked/expired transfers, actionable MCP resource errors or CSRF failure. Review never launches a target or calls a model.
review.guidance: Works on retained recordings, including on macOS; no model credentials, capture runtime or target launch needed. Library: Showrun(storage).review_store(), then ReviewStore operations. Use one explicit workspace and optional demo scope consistently. Read state/version before selection or edits; mutations use exact identities, expected versions and request IDs. Notes never start capture. Deletion requires prepare-delete confirmation; MP4/ZIP exports preserve original media and refuse overwrite. review serve starts a local authenticated dashboard with a one-use bootstrap URL; keep it private. Use showrun review -h for operation flags.

arguments.--build: Compile locally with Apple Command Line Tools on macOS or the .NET 8 SDK on Windows instead of downloading the pinned binary.

prepare-desktop.result: Prepared app/helper paths, signing notice, release and checksum for downloaded installs; model_calls=0.
prepare-desktop.failures: Prebuilt binaries support Apple Silicon macOS 14+ and Windows x64 (tested on Windows 11). Checksum failures preserve the current binary. macOS is ad-hoc signed, not notarized; Windows is unsigned early access. Running Windows companions must close before replacement.
prepare-desktop.guidance: Explicit acquisition only; never downloads during record. Downloads the platform-pinned GitHub Release and verifies SHA-256. macOS additionally verifies the app signature and installs ~/Applications/Showrun Desktop.app; grant Accessibility and Screen & System Audio Recording (also covers output audio); Microphone only via desktop-status --request-microphone when recording a microphone. Windows installs %LOCALAPPDATA%/Showrun/Desktop/ShowrunDesktop.exe with the .NET runtime included, so no SDK or separate runtime is needed. Windows x64 is early access and unsigned. Keep the user desktop unlocked. Run desktop-status after installation. Use --build for developer compilation. Library: Showrun.prepare_desktop(build=False). The Mac pin is desktop-v0.6.0 (adds opt-in ScreenCaptureKit audio); Windows remains desktop-v0.2.0. Ad-hoc Mac updates can invalidate grants despite enabled Settings switches: remove and re-add the app in both privacy lists, then recheck desktop-status.

arguments.--request-microphone: Explicit setup: show the macOS Microphone prompt once (desktop-v0.6.0+, macOS 15+). Needed only for capture.audio.microphone; record never prompts.

desktop-status.result: macOS: ready, screen_recording, accessibility, microphone (authorized/denied/not_determined/restricted/unknown), audio={output_ready, microphone_ready, microphone_requested} and bundle_id. ready covers window capture and input only; audio readiness is separate. Windows: ready and session_id. Both return model_calls=0 and companion={version,protocol,capabilities}; missing handshake metadata is explicitly unknown, not inferred from the download pin. Readiness does not certify app-specific capture or terminal support. The desktop-v0.6.0 Mac build reports its exact version, protocol 1 and advertised capabilities; build identity does not establish publication. Older companions remain usable with unknown metadata.
desktop-status.failures: Missing app, blocked app launch, or broken local connection. No target app is inspected.
desktop-status.guidance: Launch the companion via LaunchServices and check both permission grants independently. Library: Showrun.desktop_status(request_microphone=False). Without --request-microphone it never prompts. No screenshot, target actions or inference. Exit 0 means the check completed; inspect ready for permission readiness. On Windows, returns ready and session_id from an interactive limited-privilege task under the caller account; no target is inspected.
